data_github_protected_branch_pull_reques: `github_protected_branch_pull_request_review` reads a protected branch's own required pull request review settings -- how many approvals, whether stale reviews are dismissed.
data_github_public_ip: `github_public_ip` reads GitHub's own real, currently published IP address ranges for a specific service (web, API, Actions, and similar).
data_github_pull: `github_pull` looks up a real pull request, the compact shape returned when a pull request is referenced from elsewhere rather than fetched directly.
data_github_pull_request_review_request: `github_pull_request_review_request` looks up which real reviewers or teams are currently requested on an open pull request, part of the same real pull request `github_pull_request` represents as a whole.
data_github_rate_limit_overview: `github_rate_limit_overview` reads the real, current REST and GraphQL API rate limit status for the authenticated caller -- how many requests remain before the next reset.
data_github_release: `github_release` looks up one real, already-published point in a repository's history, built on a specific git tag, with its own release notes and binary files.
data_github_release_asset: `github_release_asset` looks up one real file already attached to a release beyond the zip and tarball archives GitHub generates automatically.
data_github_repo: `github_repo` lists the real repositories an organization or user actually owns, with real filters for creation, visibility, and archive status -- the search/listing counterpart to looking up one `github_full_repository` by name.
data_github_repo_codespaces_secret: `github_repo_codespaces_secret` looks up the real metadata of a repository-level Codespaces secret -- never its own decrypted value.
data_github_repo_search_result_item: `github_repo_search_result_item` looks up one real match from a GitHub repository search.
data_github_repository: `github_repository` looks up the complete, real record of a repository -- code, files, revision history, and every setting attached to it.
data_github_repository_collaborator_perm: `github_repository_collaborator_permission` reads a specific real collaborator's own current permission level on a repository.
data_github_repository_hash_algorithm: `github_repository_hash_algorithm` reads which real Git object hash algorithm (SHA-1 or SHA-256) a repository was created with.
data_github_repository_ruleset: `github_repository_ruleset` looks up a real, already-defined named set of rules applied to one or many branches or tags via a pattern.
data_github_repository_subscription: `github_repository_subscription` reads whether the authenticated user is currently watching a repository, and whether notifications are muted.
data_github_required_status_check: `github_required_status_check` reads which specific status check contexts a branch's own protection rule currently requires to pass before a merge is allowed.
data_github_resource: `github_resource` looks up a real, published security advisory's own affected package and vulnerable version range.
data_github_restriction: `github_restriction` reads a protected branch's own current push restrictions -- which users, teams, or apps are allowed to push directly.
data_github_review: `github_review` looks up one real, already-submitted pull request review -- its own state (approved, changes requested, commented) and body.
data_github_root: `github_root` reads the real root of the GitHub REST API -- the top-level map of URL templates every other real endpoint hangs off of.
data_github_rule_suite: `github_rule_suite` looks up one real, already-evaluated ruleset run against a specific push -- which rules passed or failed.
data_github_rule_suites: `github_rule_suites` lists the real ruleset evaluation runs already recorded for a repository or organization.
data_github_ruleset: `github_ruleset` looks up a real, already-defined repository or organization ruleset and its own current rules.
data_github_ruleset_version_with_state: `github_ruleset_version_with_state` looks up one real, historical version of a ruleset, along with whether it was active at that time.
data_github_run: `github_run` looks up a real Actions workflow run -- its own status, conclusion, and the commit that triggered it.
data_github_runner: `github_runner` looks up a real, already-registered self-hosted Actions runner and its own current online/offline status.
data_github_runner_groups_enterprise: `github_runner_groups_enterprise` looks up a real, already-configured named collection of self-hosted GitHub Actions runners managed at the enterprise level and shared across member organizations.
data_github_runner_groups_org: `github_runner_groups_org` looks up a real, already-configured collection of self-hosted runners at the organization level, along with which repositories are allowed to use them.
data_github_runner_label: `github_runner_label` looks up a real, custom label already attached to a self-hosted runner, used to target workflow jobs at it.
data_github_sbom: `github_sbom` exports a repository's own real, current dependency graph as an SPDX-format software bill of materials, the same real export `github_dependency_graph_spdx_sbom` provides.
data_github_scim_enterprise_group_respon: `github_scim_enterprise_group_response` looks up a real, SCIM-provisioned group at the enterprise level, kept in sync by the enterprise's own identity provider.
data_github_scim_enterprise_user_respons: `github_scim_enterprise_user_response` looks up a real, SCIM-provisioned enterprise member's own identity attributes as synced from the enterprise's identity provider.
data_github_scim_user: `github_scim_user` looks up a real, SCIM-provisioned organization member, synced by the organization's own connected identity provider rather than an enterprise-wide one.
data_github_secret_scanning: `github_secret_scanning` reads a repository's own real, current secret scanning configuration and enablement status.
data_github_secret_scanning_alert_with_m: `github_secret_scanning_alert_with_metadata` looks up one real secret scanning finding -- the detected secret type, its own state, and push-protection bypass details if any.
data_github_secret_scanning_pattern_conf: `github_secret_scanning_pattern_configuration` reads which real secret scanning detection patterns are currently enabled for a repository or organization.
data_github_selected_actions: `github_selected_actions` reads which specific actions and reusable workflows are currently allowlisted to run, when a repository or organization restricts Actions to a selected list rather than allowing all of them.
data_github_self_hosted_runners_settings: `github_self_hosted_runners_settings` reads an organization or enterprise's own real policy for which repositories are allowed to register self-hosted runners.
data_github_server_statistics: `github_server_statistics` reads real, aggregated usage statistics for a GitHub Enterprise Server instance.
data_github_simple_commit_status: `github_simple_commit_status` looks up one real, already-reported commit status -- its own state, context, and description.
data_github_simple_user: `github_simple_user` looks up the minimal, real identity record behind a GitHub account -- username, ID, avatar, profile URL -- without pulling the account's entire full record.
data_github_stargazer: `github_stargazer` looks up a real user who has starred a repository, and when they did.
data_github_stat: `github_stat` reads a real, aggregated repository statistic -- one of the real code-frequency, commit-activity, or contributor-count views GitHub computes and caches for a repository.
data_github_statu: `github_statu` reads the real, current status of an in-progress enterprise migration job.
data_github_status_check_policy: `github_status_check_policy` reads a protected branch's own currently required status checks -- which context names must report success before a merge is allowed.
data_github_stubbed: `github_stubbed` is a paginated placeholder shape carried in the real API schema with no further real, distinguishing field content beyond pagination -- not a business-domain lookup like the rest of this reference.
data_github_task: `github_task` looks up one real repository's own already-recorded result within a broader Multi-Repository Variant Analysis run -- its analysis status, its result count, and the reason it failed if it did.
data_github_team: `github_team` looks up a real team's own compact profile, the shape returned when a team is referenced from elsewhere rather than fetched directly.
data_github_team_full: `github_team_full` looks up a real, already-created group of organization members, along with the access permissions that cascade down through any nested teams.
data_github_team_membership: `github_team_membership` looks up one real person's own already-established place inside a team -- member or maintainer.
data_github_team_repository: `github_team_repository` reads which real permission level a specific team has been granted on a specific repository.
data_github_thread: `github_thread` looks up a real notification thread -- the issue, pull request, or discussion it's about, and whether it's been read.
data_github_thread_subscription: `github_thread_subscription` reads whether the authenticated user is currently subscribed to a specific notification thread.
data_github_topic: `github_topic` reads the real list of topics currently attached to a repository.
data_github_topic_search_result_item: `github_topic_search_result_item` looks up one real match from a GitHub topic search.
data_github_traffic: `github_traffic` reads a repository's own real visitor and clone counts over the last 14 days, from repository traffic analytics.
data_github_user: `github_user` looks up a real GitHub user's own full public profile.
data_github_user_search_result_item: `github_user_search_result_item` looks up one real match from a GitHub user search.
data_github_view: `github_view` looks up a real, already-configured view (a filtered, sorted layout) on a Projects (v2) board.
data_github_visual_studio_subscription_a: `github_visual_studio_subscription_assignment` reads whether a specific user's own GitHub Enterprise access is currently granted through a Visual Studio subscription benefit.
data_github_vulnerability: `github_vulnerability` looks up one real, specific vulnerable version range within a published security advisory.
data_github_webhook_config: `github_webhook_config` reads a repository or organization webhook's own current delivery configuration -- its target URL, content type, and secret status.
data_github_workflow: `github_workflow` looks up a real Actions workflow file already defined in a repository -- its own name, path, and current enabled/disabled state.
data_github_workflow_run: `github_workflow_run` looks up a real Actions workflow run, the same real run `github_run` represents.
github_actions_hosted_runner: `github_actions_hosted_runner` is a virtual machine GitHub provisions and maintains to run one Actions job -- Ubuntu, Windows, or macOS, with maintenance and OS upgrades handled automatically. Standard GitHub-hosted runners are free and unlimited on public repositories; private repositories consume the account's own included minutes, then bill per minute.
github_actions_secret: `github_actions_secret` creates or updates an encrypted secret available to GitHub Actions workflows in a repository, referenced by name from a workflow's own `secrets` context.
github_actions_variable: `github_actions_variable` stores non-sensitive configuration -- a compiler flag, a hostname, anything safe to appear unmasked in a build log -- reused across workflows via the `vars` context. It's the deliberate counterpart to a secret: secrets are encrypted client-side before reaching GitHub and must be explicitly referenced to be read; variables carry no such protection because they were never meant to hold anything sensitive.
github_attestation: `github_attestation` is a cryptographically signed record establishing where and how a real software artifact was built -- the real supply-chain-security mechanism for proving a binary or container image's own build provenance, so anyone consuming it can verify it actually came from the build it claims to.
github_autolink: `github_autolink` configures a pattern that automatically converts references to an external system -- a JIRA issue, a Zendesk ticket -- into a real clickable link anywhere that pattern appears in a repository's issues, pull requests, and commit messages, without needing to write the full URL out every time.
github_blob: `github_blob` is a raw git object holding one file's own content at a specific point in history, addressed by its own SHA rather than a filename or path -- the lowest-level building block a git tree assembles into a real directory structure.
github_branch_with_protection: `github_branch_with_protection` enforces real requirements on a specific branch, a name pattern, or every branch in a repository -- passing status checks, an approving review, a linear history -- and can block force pushes or deletion outright. It's the mechanism that turns "please don't break main" into something GitHub actually enforces rather than a convention people can ignore.
github_campaign_summary: `github_campaign_summary` groups a real set of code scanning or secret scanning alerts into one trackable effort, shared with the developers who need to fix them. Code-scanning campaigns automatically trigger Copilot Autofix for every included alert, and a campaign's own tracking view shows real progress toward remediation across however many repositories it spans.
github_check_run: `github_check_run` is one individual test result inside a check suite, created and updated by a GitHub App as it moves through `queued`, `in_progress`, and `completed` -- the real, per-test granularity behind a pull request's own status checks.
github_check_suite: `github_check_suite` is the real collection of every check run one GitHub App created for a single commit, automatically created the moment that commit is pushed -- the grouping check runs belong to, not something created directly on its own.
github_code_scanning_sarifs_status: `github_code_scanning_sarifs_status` reports whether an uploaded SARIF results file has finished processing -- code scanning expects one such upload per analysis, and this is the real, honest way to confirm a given upload actually succeeded rather than assuming it did.
github_code_scanning_variant_analysis: `github_code_scanning_variant_analysis` runs one CodeQL query against up to 1,000 real repositories at once (Multi-Repository Variant Analysis), scaling a single known vulnerability pattern into a search across every codebase that might share it, rather than checking one repository at a time.
github_code_security_configuration: `github_code_security_configuration` bundles real security features -- Dependabot alerts, CodeQL code scanning, secret protection -- into one named, centrally-managed policy an organization can apply across many repositories at once, instead of enabling each feature repository by repository.
github_codespace: `github_codespace` is a cloud-hosted development environment running in a real Docker container, reachable from a browser, VS Code, or the GitHub CLI with no local setup at all. Organizations customize the container itself via configuration files, so every codespace for a project starts from the same real, consistent environment.
github_codespace_export_details: `github_codespace_export_details` tracks the real, asynchronous process of pushing a codespace's own uncommitted changes out to a new branch -- the mechanism for recovering real work done in a codespace that's about to be deleted without a normal commit ever having been made.
github_codespaces_org_secret: `github_codespaces_org_secret` creates or updates an encrypted secret available to Codespaces for repositories within an organization, scoped to a caller-chosen selection of them.
github_codespaces_secret: `github_codespaces_secret` creates or updates an encrypted secret available to a user's own Codespaces across every repository they create one in.
github_commit: `github_commit` is one real, immutable snapshot of a repository at a point in time -- an author, a message, a parent commit (or commits, for a merge), and the tree of file contents that snapshot actually contains.
github_commit_comment: `github_commit_comment` is a comment attached directly to one specific commit, independent of any pull request or issue -- real feedback tied to the exact change that prompted it, viewable and manageable through the same real API as any other GitHub comment.
github_content: `github_content` creates or updates a file's own real contents in a repository, committing the change directly to a branch.
github_copilot_space: `github_copilot_space` organizes real context -- repositories, code, pull requests, issues, free-text notes, images -- that grounds Copilot's own answers in the specific project or task a space was built for. Spaces stay in sync as the underlying GitHub content changes, and can belong to a personal account or an organization, shared with a team or made public.
github_copilot_space_resource: `github_copilot_space_resource` is one real piece of content -- a repository, a file, a pull request, a note -- added into a Copilot Space, the individual unit a space's own context is actually built from.
github_custom_property: `github_custom_property` is a structured metadata field an organization defines and attaches to its own repositories -- text, a single or multi-select value, or a boolean -- used to target repositories with rulesets and drive real governance and automation without relying on naming conventions alone.
github_dependabot_alert_dismissal_reques: `github_dependabot_alert_dismissal_request` is a real, tracked request to dismiss a Dependabot security alert on a repository -- who asked for the dismissal, why (a stated reason like "tolerable risk" or "not used in production"), and the review responses it received. It exists as its own resource because dismissing an alert in a governed organization is a workflow with an audit trail, not a single-click state flip.
github_dependabot_secret: `github_dependabot_secret` creates or updates an encrypted secret available to Dependabot version updates in a repository, referenced by name from a manifest's own registry configuration.
github_deploy_key: `github_deploy_key` is an SSH key attached directly to one repository rather than to a personal account -- the public half lives on the repository, the private half stays on the server that needs access, with no expiration date, making it the real fit for automated deployments that shouldn't depend on any one person's own credentials.
github_deployment: `github_deployment` is a real request to deploy a specific ref -- a branch, a SHA, a tag -- that GitHub turns into a `deployment` event external services can listen for and act on, the API-level record of a deployment actually having been requested.
github_deployment_branch_policy: `github_deployment_branch_policy` restricts which branches are even allowed to deploy to a given environment, matched by a real custom name pattern -- the guardrail that stops an arbitrary branch from ever reaching a protected environment by accident.
github_deployment_protection_rule: `github_deployment_protection_rule` is a real, custom gate a deployment to a protected environment must pass before it's allowed to proceed -- configured, created, and deleted through the same API, giving an external system its own say in whether a deployment continues.
github_deployment_status: `github_deployment_status` marks one deployment's own real outcome -- `pending`, `in_progress`, `success`, `failure`, `error`, `queued` -- and is what a `deployment_status` webhook subscriber actually consumes to know whether a deployment it triggered succeeded.
github_enterprise_team: `github_enterprise_team` is a team defined once at the enterprise level and assignable across up to 15,000 organizations within it, rather than being recreated separately inside every organization -- real, centralized team management at a scale a single organization's own teams were never meant to cover.
github_environment: `github_environment` is a named deployment target -- staging, production -- that a workflow job references, and which can enforce real protection rules (required approvers, wait timers, branch restrictions) before the job is allowed to run or read that environment's own secrets.
github_full_repository: `github_full_repository` is the complete, real record of a repository -- code, files, and their revision history -- along with every setting and permission attached to it, the base unit almost every other GitHub resource in this reference is scoped underneath.
github_get_audit_log_stream_config: `github_get_audit_log_stream_config` is one configured destination an enterprise streams its GitHub audit log events to in near-real-time -- Splunk, Datadog, Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, and similar SIEM/log-aggregation targets are real, supported vendors. Enterprises with this configured get continuous audit log delivery instead of relying on the paginated REST/UI audit log alone.
github_get_budget: `github_get_budget` reads back one organization- or enterprise-level spending budget -- its own amount, its own alert thresholds -- part of GitHub's real billing API for programmatically managing the full lifecycle of a budget rather than only viewing usage after the fact.
github_get_cost_center: `github_get_cost_center` is an enterprise's own real billing grouping -- a named bucket (mapped to an Azure subscription, a set of users, or a set of resources) that GitHub's own cost-management reporting attributes spend to, letting a large organization break down its GitHub bill by team or department rather than reading one undifferentiated enterprise total.
github_gist_comment: `github_gist_comment` is a comment left on a real gist, the same real commenting mechanism GitHub uses on issues and commits, applied to a shared code snippet instead.
github_gist_simple: `github_gist_simple` is a real, shareable code snippet that's actually its own git repository underneath -- forkable and clonable like any other -- published either public (discoverable and searchable) or secret (reachable only by anyone who has the exact URL).
github_git_commit: `github_git_commit` is the raw git commit object itself -- author, message, parent SHA, and the tree it points at -- accessed directly through the Git Data API rather than through the higher-level commit resource most workflows use day to day.
github_git_ref: `github_git_ref` is a named pointer -- a branch head or a tag -- to a specific real commit, the real object that moves forward every time a branch gets a new commit.
github_git_tag: `github_git_tag` is a real, named marker attached to one specific commit, typically used for a release or another point worth being able to find again without walking the commit history to locate it.
github_git_tree: `github_git_tree` represents the real directory structure and file contents of a repository at one specific point in its history -- what a commit object actually points at to say what the repository looked like right then.
github_gpg_key: `github_gpg_key` signs commits and tags with real, verifiable cryptographic proof of who actually authored them, and unlike an SSH key used the same way, a GPG key supports real expiration and revocation -- lifecycle management SSH signing has no equivalent for.
github_hook: `github_hook` (a repository webhook) delivers real event data to an external server the moment a subscribed event happens on that repository -- a push, an issue opened, a pull request merged -- the mechanism behind triggering an external CI pipeline, a deployment, or a notification without polling GitHub for changes.
github_installation: `github_installation` is a real, live installation of a GitHub App on a user account, organization, or enterprise -- which repositories it can see, which permissions it was granted, and the credentials (access_tokens_url, client_id) GitHub issues for it to act with. Every GitHub App integration, from a CI bot to a security scanner, is represented on GitHub's own side by exactly one of these per account it's installed on.
github_issue: `github_issue` tracks a real unit of work -- a bug report, a feature idea, anything worth writing down and discussing -- inside a repository, with support for sub-issues, dependencies between issues, and integration with pull requests that close them automatically.
github_issue_comment: `github_issue_comment` is one comment in the real, ongoing discussion thread attached to an issue -- the same real commenting mechanism issues share with pull requests and commits, applied to whatever conversation an issue itself is tracking.
github_job: `github_job` is one real unit of work within an Actions workflow run -- a set of steps executed together on the same runner -- the actual thing a runner (hosted or self-hosted) picks up and works through from start to finish.
github_key: `github_key` is an SSH public key added to a personal account for authentication -- what actually lets `git push`/`git pull` over SSH identify a specific real user, distinct from a deploy key's own repository-only scope.
github_label: `github_label` categorizes issues, pull requests, and discussions inside a repository -- a real, lightweight classification tool for organizing and filtering work rather than hunting through everything unsorted.
github_migration: `github_migration` is a real, in-progress or completed transfer of repository (or, from GitHub.com, whole-organization) data into GitHub Enterprise Cloud via GitHub Enterprise Importer -- the API-driven path for advanced migrations too customized for the CLI tool most customers use instead.
github_milestone: `github_milestone` groups a real set of issues or pull requests toward one shared target -- a due date, a completion percentage tracked automatically as items in it open and close -- the mechanism for watching a body of related work move toward done rather than tracking each item in isolation.
github_network_configuration: `github_network_configuration` is the real, organization- or enterprise-level construct that governs private networking for GitHub-hosted compute -- controlling outbound access, routing runner traffic through a private Azure VNet, and optionally a real failover subnet if the primary one becomes unavailable.
github_org_hook: `github_org_hook` is a webhook scoped to an entire organization rather than one repository -- the same real event-delivery mechanism, applied once at the org level instead of being configured separately on every repository inside it.
github_org_membership: `github_org_membership` records one real user's own role inside an organization -- `admin` (owner-level access) or `member` (everything else) -- and only an existing organization owner can create or change it; promoting someone to admin sends them a real notification email, demoting an owner does not.
github_org_private_registry_configuratio: `github_org_private_registry_configuration` stores the real credentials an organization's own Actions workflows use to pull from a private package registry -- npm, Docker, or another supported registry -- configured once centrally rather than duplicated into every workflow that needs it.
github_organization_actions_secret: `github_organization_actions_secret` creates or updates an encrypted secret available to GitHub Actions workflows across repositories within an organization, scoped to a caller-chosen selection of them.
github_organization_actions_variable: `github_organization_actions_variable` is the same real Actions configuration-variable mechanism as a repository-level variable, defined once at the organization level so every repository underneath can read it through the `vars` context without redefining it repository by repository.
github_organization_custom_property: `github_organization_custom_property` is a custom metadata field an organization defines for its own repositories -- a name, a value type (string, single-select, multi-select, true/false), and who's allowed to edit it. Organizations use these to tag repositories with facts GitHub doesn't track natively (an internal team owner, a compliance tier, a deployment environment), then filter and govern repositories by that tag at scale.
github_organization_custom_repository_ro: `github_organization_custom_repository_role` is a repository-level permission role an organization defines on top of GitHub's own built-in roles (read/triage/write/maintain/admin) -- a named base role plus a real, granted subset of fine-grained permissions layered on it. Organizations use these when none of GitHub's own five built-in roles matches a real team's actual responsibilities.
github_organization_dependabot_secret: `github_organization_dependabot_secret` creates or updates an encrypted secret available to Dependabot version updates across repositories within an organization, scoped to a caller-chosen selection of them.
github_organization_role: `github_organization_role` is an organization-level (not repository-level) custom permission role -- what an organization owner can grant someone to manage organization settings, teams, or security configuration without handing over full organization-owner access. Distinct from `github_organization_custom_repository_role`, which scopes to a single repository rather than the whole organization.
github_organization_simple: `github_organization_simple` is a shared account real teams collaborate through -- a container with its own name and brand for repositories, projects, and members, each granted a real role that controls exactly what they can see and do inside it.
github_package: `github_package` is a real package published to GitHub Packages -- its own name, type, and visibility.
github_package_version: `github_package_version` is a real, specific version of a package already published to GitHub Packages.
github_page_build: `github_page_build` is one real run of GitHub Pages' own publish pipeline -- taking a repository's HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (optionally through Jekyll or another build tool first) and deploying the resulting static site to the web.
github_pages_deployment_status: `github_pages_deployment_status` reports the real, current state of one specific GitHub Pages deployment -- whether the latest page build actually finished publishing or is still in progress.
github_projects_v2_field: `github_projects_v2_field` is a real piece of metadata attached to items inside a Project -- a built-in field like assignee, or a custom one like priority -- adding context beyond what an issue or pull request already carries on its own, up to 50 fields per project.
github_projects_v2_item_with_content: `github_projects_v2_item_with_content` is one real entry inside a Project -- an issue, a pull request, or a draft issue -- together with the real content it's actually tracking, the unit a project's own views, fields, and automation all operate on.
github_pull_request: `github_pull_request` proposes merging one branch's own changes into another, GitHub's real, central collaboration feature for discussing and reviewing code before it lands -- conversation, commits, checks, and file diffs all attached to the same real proposal.
github_pull_request_merge_async_result: `github_pull_request_merge_async_result` is the real, polled outcome of a pull request merge that GitHub processes asynchronously rather than completing inline -- checked after the fact to confirm whether the merge actually succeeded.
github_pull_request_review: `github_pull_request_review` is a real, submitted verdict on a pull request's own changes -- approve, request changes, or comment -- the structured mechanism that turns informal feedback into an actual, trackable review a repository's own rules can require before merging.
github_pull_request_review_comment: `github_pull_request_review_comment` is a comment attached to one specific line of a pull request's own diff, part of a real review rather than the general conversation thread -- feedback tied to the exact code it's about.
github_release: `github_release` packages one real point in a repository's history -- built on a specific git tag -- with release notes and binary files, the deployable, citable unit a repository's own users actually download and install.
github_release_asset: `github_release_asset` is one real file attached to a release beyond the zip and tarball archives GitHub generates automatically -- up to 1,000 additional files per release, each under 2 GiB, for shipping compiled binaries or other build output alongside the source.
github_repo_codespaces_secret: `github_repo_codespaces_secret` creates or updates an encrypted secret available to Codespaces created from a specific repository.
github_repository_advisory: `github_repository_advisory` is a private, real space for a repository's own maintainers and a vulnerability reporter to discuss, fix, and prepare a security issue before it's ever disclosed publicly -- published only once a real patch is actually ready.
github_repository_ruleset: `github_repository_ruleset` is a named, real set of rules -- who can push to a branch, how commits must be formatted, who can delete a tag -- applied to one or many branches or tags via a pattern, and unlike a classic branch protection rule, a ruleset can also apply across every repository in an organization at once, up to 75 per repository.
github_runner_groups_enterprise: `github_runner_groups_enterprise` is a named collection of self-hosted GitHub Actions runners managed at the enterprise level and shared across member organizations -- which organizations and workflows may use the group, and whether it's restricted to specific workflow files. Enterprises use runner groups to control which teams can run jobs on which hardware, rather than every organization managing its own separate runner pool.
github_runner_groups_org: `github_runner_groups_org` controls real access to a set of self-hosted runners at the organization level -- every organization starts with one default group, and access policies on a custom group decide which repositories are even allowed to use the runners inside it.
github_scim_enterprise_group_response: `github_scim_enterprise_group_response` is a SCIM-provisioned group at the enterprise level -- its display name, external ID from the identity provider, and real member list -- kept in sync by an enterprise's own SSO/identity provider (Okta, Azure AD, and similar) rather than managed by hand inside GitHub. Enterprises with SCIM provisioning enabled use groups like this to drive automatic team membership from their own IdP.
github_scim_enterprise_user_response: `github_scim_enterprise_user_response` is a SCIM-provisioned enterprise member -- their real identity attributes (name, emails, roles, active status) as synced from the enterprise's own identity provider, the standard mechanism large organizations use to add, update, and deactivate GitHub access automatically as employees join, move, or leave.
github_scim_user: `github_scim_user` is a SCIM-provisioned organization member -- the org-scoped counterpart to `github_scim_enterprise_user_response`, synced by an organization's own connected identity provider rather than the enterprise-wide one. Represents one real person's provisioned GitHub organization membership and its current active/inactive state.
github_simple_user: `github_simple_user` is the minimal, real identity record behind a GitHub account -- username, ID, avatar, profile URL -- the compact shape GitHub's own API returns whenever a resource needs to reference a user without pulling their entire, full account record.
github_ssh_signing_key: `github_ssh_signing_key` is an SSH key used to sign commits and tags rather than to authenticate -- functionally the same kind of key as one used for `git push`, and the same key can genuinely serve both roles, added here specifically as a signing key with no real limit on how many an account can have.
github_stack: `github_stack` records where one pull request sits inside a real stack -- a chain of smaller, dependent pull requests, each showing only its own layer's diff instead of one large change. Stacks merge from the bottom up, and any contiguous run of pull requests starting from the lowest unmerged one can be merged together at once.
github_task: `github_task` is one real repository's own result within a broader Multi-Repository Variant Analysis run -- its analysis status, its result count once finished, and the reason it failed if it did -- the per-repository record a variant analysis run is actually made up of.
github_team_full: `github_team_full` is a real group of organization members reflecting a company's own structure, with access permissions that cascade down through nested teams -- the mechanism for granting repository access to a whole group at once instead of adding people individually.
github_team_membership: `github_team_membership` records one real person's own place inside a team -- member or maintainer -- which is what actually determines whether they inherit that team's own repository permissions and get included in its notifications and review requests.
github_team_repository: `github_team_repository` grants a team access to a repository at a specific permission level, adding the repository to the team's own list of managed repositories.
github_usage_report_export: `github_usage_report_export` is a requested, generated export of an enterprise's own GitHub Actions/Packages/Copilot usage data over a real date range -- its status, the actor who requested it, and the download URLs for the finished report. Enterprises use these for real cost attribution and usage auditing beyond what the live billing dashboard shows.
